title: Paradiso source-grounding metadata model (SourceRecord / EvidenceRecord / AnswerGrounding)
purpose: Formalize the three durable grounding concepts the platform already expresses
in scattered, inconsistently-named fields across several JSON files and the
runtime AskResponse model. This file introduces NO new runtime contract: it
is a canonical vocabulary plus a field crosswalk so audits and CI can reason
about source freshness, evidence lineage, and per-answer grounding uniformly.
It is validated by scripts/check_source_grounding_metadata.py and the test
/api/ask and changing it never alters answer behavior.

SourceRecord.description: An official source the platform relies on (a manual PDF, a law/regulation, a public API, an official web page, or an internal-review decision).

canonical_fields.title: human title (Korean authoritative; English optional helper)
canonical_fields.issuing_authority: the body that publishes the source
canonical_fields.official_url: canonical official URL (may be null for offline PDFs)
canonical_fields.retrieved_at: ISO8601 timestamp the source was last fetched/checked (nullable)
canonical_fields.published_or_updated_at: ISO8601 date the source itself was published/updated
canonical_fields.hash_or_etag: content hash or HTTP ETag for drift detection (nullable)

EvidenceRecord.description: A specific excerpt/binding that ties a visa-or-status code + topic to a SourceRecord, with a precise location and a normalized summary.

canonical_fields.id: stable string id (may be synthesized from code+source+section)
canonical_fields.source_id: id of the SourceRecord this evidence comes from
canonical_fields.excerpt: verbatim or close source excerpt (never invented)
canonical_fields.location_reference: page, section, article, route, or URL fragment
canonical_fields.normalized_summary: neutral paraphrase used for prompt context
canonical_fields.last_verified_at: ISO8601 timestamp of last human/automated verification

AnswerGrounding.description: Per-answer grounding lineage. Currently COMPUTED at runtime by /api/ask and surfaced on AskResponse; it is not persisted. The field map below shows where each canonical concept already lives.

canonical_fields.answer_id_or_request_id: stable id for the generated answer/request
canonical_fields.cited_evidence_ids: evidence/source ids actually used to ground the answer
canonical_fields.missing_evidence_flags: markers for evidence that was sought but unavailable
canonical_fields.uncertainty_flags: markers that force hedged / confirmation-required language
canonical_fields.prohibited_claim_flags: markers for claims the answer must not assert
canonical_fields.generated_at: ISO8601 timestamp the answer was produced

field_crosswalk.note: Maps the canonical SourceRecord/EvidenceRecord field names to the real field names used across existing files. Validators use this to read heterogeneous files uniformly.

answer_id_or_request_id: (not persisted; add request_id to AskResponse to populate)
prohibited_claim_flags: (enforced via prompt confidence-gate + post-answer quality gate; not a single stored field)
generated_at: (response time; add to AskResponse to persist)

manual_version_invariants.note: Asserted by the validator + test against data/source_registry.json and docs/source-manuals/source_manifest.json. Update intentionally when a new official manual is installed.

rules: If an active SourceRecord hash_or_etag disagrees between data/source_registry.json and docs/source-manuals/source_manifest.json, that is hard drift (validator error).
If a registry active-manual published_or_updated_at is older than the manifest current source_date, emit STALE_SOURCE_WARNING.
retrieved_at / confidence / language / review_status fields that are null on official manuals are reported as freshness gaps (warning), not errors.
